title: Halcom's only recorded platforms are its own payments and e-signature products
content:
The tool field for Halcom names no partner platform at all — it records the firm's own payments and e-signature products. Its v2 verticals are banking and payments, so the products and the sectors line up: this is a company selling its own software into the market it knows.

That matters for how the priority-4 rank should be read. The rank came from a mechanical rescore of a provisional v2 tail row using size and slot occupancy, and where the platform slot is occupied by a firm's own IP, occupancy is not a temporary condition that a good pitch resolves. It is the business model. The flag consequently defers to an OSS-portfolio screen before anything is acted on.

Commercially, a payments and e-signature vendor in banking is more plausibly a counterparty than a delivery channel: any component it adopted would have to earn a place on its own product roadmap. Confirming which of those two relationships is available is the point of running the screen first.
